changes.old: Any shortfall is paid as a penalty into escrow and returned only if the clinic reaches 90% within five years.
changes.new: Any shortfall is paid as a penalty into escrow. It is returned only if the clinic reaches 90% within five years and agrees with the Department of Public Health on a plan to spend it on patient services. The department can grant one-year waivers.
changes.officialQuote: Legal text H&S Sec. 1234.5: moneys "held in escrow for a period of five years", reimbursed only if the clinic meets 90 percent and agrees a spending plan with the Department of Public Health; (c) "a temporary pause of the 90 percent requirement".

changes.old: It also bars citizen initiatives from adding local property taxes beyond what the state constitution already allows.
changes.new: It also says no local government, including voters using the initiative, may impose ad valorem taxes on real property except as Article XIII D, Section 3(a)(1) of the state constitution allows. The official analysis does not discuss this clause.
changes.officialQuote: Legal text Sec. 4.5(b): "no local government, including the electorate of a local government exercising the initiative power, may impose ad valorem taxes on real property, except as provided in paragraph (1) of subdivision (a) of Section 3 of Article XIII D."
